thread:
Jordan (Support): FYI customer SparrowInc reported a sudden throughput drop + 5xxs on our hosted API during their morning spike, started ~08:10 PT. They say responses time out and requests get 503s.
Sam (Sales): Uh oh, Sparrow is on our enterprise pilot with a 99.9% availability commit. They just escalated. cc @Priya (PM) — can we triage quickly?
Priya (PM): Thanks Jordan. Can you paste the minimal repro (route + model + payload size)? Need to know if this is a routing/policy or a runtime perf issue. Priority: decide rollback vs workaround.
Jordan (Support): Repro from customer: POST /v1/generate model: gpt-large-quant, avg seq=512, batch size ~1, concurrency 160 from their system. They reported p95 latency jumped to ~2.4s and error rate ~8%. Attached snippet from their client: 
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/json
{ "model": "gpt-large-quant", "input": "<500 tokens>" }
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{ "error": "instance overload" }
```
Alex (Eng): Thanks. First pass: that model+seq and concurrency sounds like KV cache pressure + autoscaler churn. I see correlated node evictions around that timeframe in EU region. Linking grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abc123/throughput?from=2276543000&to=2276543600
Marta (Oncall): Confirming. I observed transient GPU OOMs on pool-8 and subsequent scheduler retries. Logs: pool-8 kubelet OOMKilled -> pods restarted -> backlog.
deploybot: New deploy 2026-07-18T08:05 -> version v2026.7.18.08 applied to pool-8
Sam (Sales): Is this deploy the trigger? Sparrow said the regression started right after a deploy window. They want either rollback or guaranteed mitigation ASAP.
Alex (Eng): It aligns. v2026.7.18.08 changed kernel scheduling heuristics for large KV caches. We rolled out a heuristic that can spike memory in corner cases. Hypothesis: combined with high concurrency it pushes OOM threshold.
Priya (PM): Two parallel asks: (1) immediate mitigation to stabilize customer (rollback, route to dedicated, throttle) (2) long-term fix + launch criteria for the rollback release. Sam, what does Sparrow prefer?
Sam (Sales): They want minimal downtime. Preferred: move them to dedicated capacity or force fallback to gpt-large-fp16 variant until fix. If we must rollback, they accept as long as we communicate ETA.
Alex (Eng): Quick options:
- Option A: Hot-route Sparrow to Dedicated pool (if capacity available) — low code, takes ~15-30m ops work, preserves performance.
- Option B: Force model variant fallback to `gpt-large-fp16` on their route via routing policy — trivial config change, reduces mem footprint, may alter outputs slightly.
- Option C: Full rollback of kernel heuristic (risky for other customers, ~1h ops).
Marta (Oncall): Dedicated pool has headroom in us-west-2, but Sparrow is EU. Cross-region adds latency; we can spin up dedicated in eu-west-1 but provisioning will take ~40-60m.
Jordan (Support): Sparrow says they can tolerate a short config change; they prefer fallback to fp16 if quality delta is acceptable. They asked for a canary test first.
Priya (PM): Decision: try Option B first (fallback to fp16) + canary for 50 requests, monitor p95 and error rate for 10m. If still bad, Option A (route to dedicated) as fallback. Action owners: Alex to apply routing override + canary, Marta to monitor infra, Jordan to coordinate with Sparrow, Sam to set communications.
Alex (Eng): On it. Patch to route override: `PATCH /v1/routes/sparrowinc` body: `{ "model_override": "gpt-large-fp16", "canary": 50 }` doing now.
Marta (Oncall): Watching grafana and node logs. Alert rule: `sparrowinc_route_errors > 3% for 1m` will page eng-oncall.
Jordan (Support): Sent canary run to Sparrow, they confirmed 50 requests routed, initial p95 280ms, error rate 0.8% (down from 8%). They asked for 2-hour stability window after full switch.
Sam (Sales): Great. I've told Sparrow we started a fallback and are monitoring. They're happier but still want root cause and timeline.
Priya (PM): Backlog items:
- RCA ticket (P0): root cause of kernel heuristic mem spike, owner: Alex, due: 72h. Acceptance: demo repro + targeted fix + perf regression test.
- Rollback playbook update (P1): document rollback steps and comms, owner: Marta, due: 1 week.
- Routing policy: auto-fallback to compatible variant for mem-pressure (P1): product spec + quick-mitigations, owner: Priya, due: 2 sprints.
- Customer comms: status update + SLA credit assessment, owner: Sam/Jordan, due: 4h.
Alex (Eng): Created RCA draft: JIRA-9876. Short-term change: leave canary in place for 2h then flip to 100% if stable. I'll post logs + repro later today.
deploybot: JIRA-9876 created by alex (Eng)
Priya (PM): Acceptance criteria for considering this resolved to customer: 
- Sparrow p95 < 400ms sustained for 2 hours, error rate < 1%
- RCA and mitigation plan delivered and scheduled fix deployed to prod canary with no regression in benchmarks
- Customer receives status + remediation timeline
Jordan (Support): Noted. I'll schedule follow-up with Sparrow in 2 hours and update ticket.
Sam (Sales): Can we get an interim note to legal/finance about potential SLA credit risk? Putting a note in the customer folder now.
Marta (Oncall): I'll keep the rota on standby in case autoscaler starts churning again. If we hit >2% errors I'll escalate immediately.
Priya (PM): Thanks all. I'll create a product backlog epic for the routing fallback feature and link JIRA-9876. If Option B fails during canary we'll trigger Option A and Sam will notify Sparrow. :thumbsup:
Alex (Eng): Canary looks good at 50 -> promoting to 100% now.
Jordan (Support): Sparrow confirms 100% is now routed, p95 stable ~350ms, errors down to 0.6%. They asked to keep them posted hourly for next 4 hours.
Sam (Sales): Noted. I'll send hourly check-ins. Thanks team. :rocket:
